sentences.text: Penghusuchus is an extinct genus of gavialid crocodilian.
This animal was a medium-sized crocodilian with an estimated total length of 4.5 meters.
A large seventh maxillary tooth is a unique shared feature found in Penghusuchus, Toyotamaphimeia, and Hanyusuchus.
An excavator driver named Mr. Ming-Kuo Pan discovered a nearly complete skeleton of Penghusuchus on the coast of Neian, Penghu Islands, on March 25, 2006.
The genus name Penghusuchus refers to the Penghu Islands where it was found, while the species name honors its discoverer, Mr. Ming-Kuo Pan.
The holotype specimen of Penghusuchus represents an individual that had reached sexual maturity, indicated by the closure of neurocentral sutures in its precaudal vertebrae.
Penghusuchus is thought to be related to the fossil Asian gavialids Toyotamaphimeia from Japan and Hanyusuchus from South China.
Penghusuchus shares mosaic features of both tomistomine and gavialid lineages, potentially filling an evolutionary gap between these two groups of long-snouted crocodilians.
Fossils of Penghusuchus have been found in Middle to Upper Miocene rocks on Penghu Island, off the coast of Taiwan.
Penghusuchus lived during the Tortonian to Messinian stages, approximately 11.63 to 5.333 million years ago.
